subject: Non-adaptive processing: subprocessor locality & proof for EU residency
messages:
From: Paul Sen <paul.sen@vitalmed.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@vitalmed.com>, VitalMed IT <it@vitalmed.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requests for operational proof: non-adaptive processing & EU residency

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move forward with the pilot, our security and legal teams have two related ask areas we need formal evidence for: (1) confirmation that Redwood will not use our tenant data for model training (non-adaptive / no-training commitment), and (2) operational proof that processing and storage for our EU-resident workloads will remain within EU boundaries (subprocessors + KMS residency).

Specifically, can you provide the following artifacts or statements we can attach to the DPA:
- A short operational attestation that production inference traffic for our account will not be used to update or fine-tune models (if this is a contractual commitment, please indicate suggested DPA language).
- Current subprocessor inventory with processing countries highlighted and the date the list was generated.
- Evidence of KMS key residency (e.g., kms config screenshot) and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
- Redacted examples of runtime logs (showing host regions / IP blocks) or a transfer map that shows where inference is executed for EU requests.
- Any SOC2/ISO artifacts or pointers to where we can validate security controls relevant to onshore processing.

We need these by COB Oct 3 to stay on track with our internal sign-offs. If some items require a call, please propose times.

Best,
Paul
Paul Sen
Head of Cloud Security, VitalMed
paul.sen@vitalmed.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Sen <paul.sen@vitalmed.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requests for operational proof: non-adaptive processing & EU residency

Paul — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a mix of contractual language, a short engineering attestation, and redacted operational artifacts. Quick notes on each ask:

- No-training commitment: Redwood offers both (a) a contractual "no-adaptive-training" commitment written into the DPA addendum and (b) an operational mode where customer data is explicitly excluded from model improvement pipelines. We can propose DPA language and also provide an ops attestation signed by our head of infra.

- Subprocessor inventory: we will export the current inventory (CSV) with processing country. Note: some GPU hosts are in multi-tenant Dedicated regions; we'll mark which workloads would be routed to EU-only pools given the account configuration.

- KMS: we can provide a screenshot of the KMS configuration showing EU-resident key region. Where customers want customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key), we support that via our Dedicated/Private options — we can note the steps.

- Redacted logs / transfer map: engineering can prepare a redacted sample (no PII) that demonstrates request routing and hostname regions.

- SOC2/ISO: pointers to our compliance portal + an extract of relevant controls.

I'll coordinate internal owners: David (ops) will produce the technical artifacts; Kimberly (legal) will draft the DPA addendum language; Marissa (CS) will own delivery and the follow-up call scheduling.

We should be able to deliver a first packet by Oct 2 (redacted artifacts + draft DPA language). If that works, we'll sync after you review.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Attachment: ops-evidence-checklist.pdf (checklist of artifacts we'll produce)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requests for operational proof: non-adaptive processing & EU residency

Adding legal context / proposed ask list for the artifacts — copying Paul in the next message once we validate the artifacts schedule.

Mina / David / Marissa — please provide or confirm the following items and (where relevant) the proposed redaction approach so we can share with VitalMed legal/security:

1) Formal attestation text: short (1–2 paragraphs) from Head of Infra stating that tenant requests for the VitalMed account are not used to update or fine-tune production models, and describing the separation between inference telemetry and model training pipelines. Provide a signed PDF.

2) DPA addendum draft: proposed clause for no-adaptive-training. Suggested starter: "Provider shall not use Customer Content to modify, fine-tune, or adapt models used for inference without Customer's prior written consent." (we can iterate).

3) Subprocessor inventory: CSV with columns [subprocessor, service, processing_countries, contract_date, security_certifications]. Redact vendor internal IDs but not locations.

4) KMS evidence: screenshot + note whether key is customer-managed. If KMS is Redwood-managed, include audit log excerpt showing key region.

5) Redacted routing/logs: provide one hour of request routing logs with IP ranges replaced by ASN or region tags (example file: redacted-kv-logs.txt). Include a simple transfer map diagram (we can export from infra docs).

6) SOC2 pointer: link to compliance portal export and contact to request specific control narratives; if VitalMed requires an on-site artifact we escalate.

7) Optional: an ops-runbook excerpt describing data retention and deletion workflow for inference cache/KV; this helps legal verify no long-term retention.

Please mark which items are "contractual" vs "operational proof" — VitalMed may want contractual language for the no-training commitment but ops artifacts for residency.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Paul Sen <paul.sen@vitalmed.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@vitalmed.com>, VitalMed IT <it@vitalmed.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requests for operational proof: non-adaptive processing & EU residency

Mina / Kimberly — excellent, thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side before you package the artifacts: 

- For the "no-adaptive-training" item, VitalMed needs this *contractual* commitment in the DPA. An ops attestation is helpful but not sufficient for procurement. Please send your proposed addendum language so our counsel can review.

- For KMS: if you provide evidence the keys are in the EU but are Redwood-managed, our security team will want to understand the access controls and the rotation policy. If a BYOK path exists for Dedicated, outline the rough timeline and any limits for pilot.

- For redacted logs: acceptable if the file includes timestamps, region tags (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), and masked instance IDs; please avoid any token/PII leakage.

- We will plan a 30-minute sync to go over artifacts and to confirm whether contract language is sufficient. Proposed times: Mon Oct 6 0900–1200 CET or Tue Oct 7 1400–1600 CET. Let us know both team availability.

If you can get the first packet by Oct 2 as Mina suggested (even if draft addendum follows shortly after), that will help accelerate procurement.

Best,
Paul
Paul Sen
Head of Cloud Security, VitalMed
paul.sen@vitalmed.com

Attachment: VitalMed-evidence-requests.xlsx (internal tracker)
